- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at 1–2% above true peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true mean reversion in 10–14 day horizons; adjust forecast to align with 18-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ true values.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 70–72, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 73.5 unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8).
